title: Dad 'held falling lamp' during his wife's labour at Stepping Hill

evidence_packet.title: Dad 'held falling lamp' during his wife's labour at Stepping Hill
evidence_packet.lead: Stepping Hill's boss says the hospital in Stockport needs "at least £400m" to tackle building issues
evidence_packet.summary: Stepping Hill's boss says the hospital in Stockport needs "at least £400m" to tackle building issues
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Dad 'held falling lamp' during his wife's labour at Stepping Hill - BBC News Image source, Jules Wilkinson Image caption, Jules Wilkinson holds up a light that he said had fallen from the maternity ward ceiling at Stepping Hill Hospital while his wife was in labour By Kevin Fitzpatrick Greater Manchester political reporter Published 1 hour ago A new father said he had to hold up a light that had fallen from the maternity ward ceiling while his baby was being born below. Jules Wilkinson said the lamp "started to unscrew itself" at Stepping Hill Hospital in Stockport, Greater Manchester, while his wife Lisa was in labour. The hospital's chief executive said Stepping Hill needed "at least £400m" to address building issues while Cheadle MP Tom Morrison said he was raising the matter in Parliament. The government said Stepping Hill was receiving tens of millions of pounds for maintenance and new buildings. Image caption, Scaffolding in the main entrance to Stepping Hill Hospital Wilkinson said: "As my wife is giving birth the lamp started to unscrew itself... almost hits the midwife in the head... and literally falls out the ceiling. "It is on one of these Anglepoise arms and it just unscrewed itself." Wilkinson told BBC North West Tonight he put the lamp on his shoulders "literally hanging on by the chord" and held on to it "for the next hour or so" until his baby had been delivered. He said the maternity suites were "getting on a bit" and recalled how the birthing pools had been out of action because of a lack of heating. But he was keen to stress that "staff are doing their best". title: Tributes paid to men killed in Cheshire van crash

evidence_packet.title: Tributes paid to men killed in Cheshire van crash
evidence_packet.lead: Two men died and two others were injured when a van crashed off a country lane in Goostrey
evidence_packet.summary: Two men died and two others were injured when a van crashed off a country lane in Goostrey
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Families have paid tribute to two men who died after a van crashed off a country lane in Cheshire Jason Clark, 53, a father of four from Runcorn, and Marlon Kent, 52, from Holmes Chapel, died after the incident in Goostrey on 3 November, Cheshire Police said Clark was described by his family as a "fun-loving and devoted dad" who supported his community, while Kent was remembered as a devoted son who "went out of his way to help others" Two other men, aged 48 and 49, were taken to hospital with serious injuries following the collision Clark's family said the "much-loved son, dad, partner, and friend" would be "deeply missed" "He leaves behind his loving parents, his two adult children, his two young children, and his devoted partner of 12 years, all of whom will forever cherish the love, laughter, and memories they shared with him," they said

evidence_packet.summary: Resident Nicha Rowson campaigned against the dump, which she calls a "monstrosity on our doorstep"
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A resident living next to a large illegal waste tip that led to rat infestations and a fire says her family can "finally move on with our lives" after work to clear the site began About 18,000 tonnes of waste began to be moved from Bolton House Road, near Bickershaw, Wigan, on Tuesday. The government-funded operation will see up to 25 lorry loads of waste removed a day and is expected to take until Spring Campaigner and resident Nicha Rowson said she was "absolutely ecstatic" but the community should not have had the smells or "this monstrosity on our doorstep" for two years Wigan Council leader Nazia Rehman thanked "everyone who has campaigned tirelessly to get us to this point" Speaking of the impact the site had had on herself and her family, Nicha said: "It's been absolutely awful - we have had rat infestations, we have had seagulls, we've had smells." She said one of her two autistic children had sensory issues, causing a heightened sense of smell from the household and commercial waste

title: War veteran returns Falklands helmet to Argentina

evidence_packet.title: War veteran returns Falklands helmet to Argentina
evidence_packet.lead: More than 40 years after the Falklands War, two veterans reunite for a new documentary
evidence_packet.summary: More than 40 years after the Falklands War, two veterans reunite for a new documentary
evidence_packet.evidence_text: War veteran returns Falklands helmet to Argentina - BBC News Image source, Mick Dawson Image caption, Andy Gatrick, right, with Hector Pereyra holding his original helmet By George Carden in Rottingdean Published 2 hours ago A former Royal Marine has reunited with an Argentine veteran to return a helmet he "borrowed" during a battle in the Falklands War. Royal Marine Andy Gatrick, who was 18 at the time, came across two injured Argentine soldiers during the Battle of Mount Harriet in 1982. The helmet belonging to one of the men, both of whom were captured by the Marines, had a name on it: Hector. Gatrick, now 63, managed to track him down and flew back on 23 October to return it. He was joined by Mick Dawson, another Royal Marine veteran from Rottingdean, East Sussex, who filmed the exchange for a new documentary called Hector's Helmet. Image source, Andy Gatrick Image caption, Royal Marine veteran Andy Gatrick, left, has returned a helmet he took during the Battle of Mount Harriet "In a very emotional day, he handed the helmet back in person to the guy he could have just as easily killed that night," said Dawson, from Rottingdean in East Sussex. Dawson, 62, told BBC Radio Sussex : "Long story short, our kit was rubbish, we had rubbish helmets that you couldn't wear. We were in berets. "They had good kit, American helmets. He borrowed one of their helmets which belonged to Hector." The two met metres from each other during the Battle of Mount Harriet, which took place on 11 and 12 June, 1982. Gatrick, from Bolton, Greater Manchester, said in footage sent to the BBC: "I put my weapon down and as I bent down to put the strap over my shoulders, I saw movement and a cloth which looked like a white handkerchief. "My eyes adjusted and there was two Argentinians, I didn't know

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Trafford Pensioner whose £20k was swiped by thief who travelled 100 miles after spotting Facebook advert speaks of ordeal 'I'm glad he's in jail' Add to preferred sources Comments News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 17:23, 10 Nov 2026 View 4 Images Dav A pensioner whose £20,000 Rolex was swiped by a thief who travelled 100 miles to his Trafford home after spotting his Facebook advert has spoken of the ordeal, saying: "I'm glad he's in jail." David Williams decided to sell his Rolex Daytona Cosmograph Oyster Perpetual watch, which he bought for £20,850 in 2023, to buy a car. The 86-year-old advertised it on Facebook for £18,000, before knocking £1,000 off He got a message from a potential buyer, 'Jack Hilmma', who said he lived in Warrington. 'Jack', who said he lived in Warrington, made a deal with David and agreed to travel to complete the sale 'Jack' was actually Tichine Asan, who lived in Hull. The 27-year-old found out David was elderly and had no relations. David said that when they met, he would be bearing a black overcoat and holding an Age UK bag They arranged the handover for December 15 last year, agreeing on a spot in Sale town centre. David said he believed it was a 'safe place'

Add to preferred sources Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 16:59, 10 Nov 2026 When Haider Ali started running the notorious Rochdale 'Adam' drugs line, he knew what he was in for. He'd already been jailed for dealing The £1m-a-year racket flooded the streets of the town with crack cocaine and heroin, surviving a series of police operations to bring it down In 2024, two 'untouchable' dealers were the latest to be jailed for running the line, first exposed in the BBC series The Detectives: Taking Down An OCG which shined a light on the gang, based in Newbold, Rochdale. The drugs line became active again within hours of the pair being Ali, 34, was a familiar face on the scene. He was jailed in 2015 after admitting conspiracy to supply heroin and cocaine - one of 13 dealers locked up following an undercover operation In its latest incarnation, Ali - known as 'The Ghost' - ran the 'Adam' line, until he and two others were caught. Monday (November 9), he was jailed for 10 years and six months

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Flames shoot into sky as fire breaks out at paper recycling plant 'At one point I thought the whole thing was going to go up' Add to preferred sources News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 16:31, 10 Nov 2026 View Image The fire broke out on at Elsa Witnesses reported seeing flames shooting into the air as a fire broke out at a paper recycling plant in Stockport . Firefighters were called to Elsa Recycling on Station Road in Reddish this morning It's thought bundles of paper being stored in the yard set alight. Plumes of black smoke were pictured billowing from the blaze Station Road is also thought to have been closed while firefighters battled the flames. Witness Rob Larkin, who works nearby, said he feared the fire was going to spread He said: "The buildings are probably 20ft high and the flames were reaching that high. At one point I thought the whole thing was going to go up "You could see it was starting to spread. A second fire developed near it, but it wasn't long before the fire brigade arrived and damped it down straight away. A second appliance turned up and they took some of the bundles which had caught fire outside

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford A 54-storey tower with 500 flats could be added to Salford's ever-changing skyline The project also includes the refurbishment of the Collier Street Baths. Add to preferred sources News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 17:48, 10 Nov 202 A new tower with more than 500 homes could soon be added to Salford ’s ever-changing skyline.Housing developer Renaker has launched plans to build Aldridge Tower, its tallest building yet in Greengate, alongside refurbishing the Grade-II listed Collier Street Baths Designed by Denton Corker Marshall, the 54-storey and 166-metre block would become a new landmark in the area off Trinity Way, which marks the border between Manchester and Salford A total of 556 ‘highly sustainable’ one and two-bedroom apartments are proposed as part of the scheme, alongside dedicated resident amenity spaces such as a pool and a gym. It also includes a landscaped public area, and the ground floor is expected to have some commercial space The plans, now open for public consultation, will build on a wider regeneration that has ‘transformed’ Greengate in recent years, with previous developments including Colliers Yard, Uptown, and GreenGate View 3 Images The lower level of the new tower block that could soon be built in Greengate. (Image: Copyright Unknown)

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A daring escape on the roof of a train. A frantic flee after Kristallnacht . A tale of survival across four concentration camps These precious stories are all contained within a collection of around 50 books that preserve the memories of Manchester’s Holocaust survivors They contain details of unspeakable brutality and unimaginable loss and trauma. They also lay bare moments of incredible courage and faith in the face of evil These captivating tales of Holocaust survival, told in the survivors' own words, will now be available to schoolchildren. The My Voice project, run by Jewish social care charity The Fed, has been launched as an educational initiative aimed at tackling antisemitism in schools acro View 4 Images Survivor Ike Alterman said: "We are the proof" when speaking about the Holocaust (Image: ABNM Photography) Raphi Bloom, The Fed’s fundraising and marketing director, says the project follows on from the horrific Manchester synagogue attack. “We approached Manchester Council and said 'how can we use the incredible lessons of our survivors?',” he said, during the launch at Star Radcliff

David Williams decided to sell his Rolex Daytona Cosmograph Oyster Perpetual watch, which he bought for £20,850 in 2023, to buy a car. The 86-year-old advertised it on Facebook for £18,000, before knocking £1,000 off He got a message from a potential buyer, 'Jack Hilmma', who said he lived in Warrington. 'Jack', who said he lived in Warrington, made a deal with David and agreed to travel to complete the sale 'Jack' was actually Tichine Asan, who lived in Hull. The 27-year-old found out David was elderly and had no relations. Donna Glynn was caught when police - acting on a tip-off - found nearly £10,000 in cash in a book She claimed her ex-partner was a drug user and that she didn't know, denying her crimes and going to trial. Some of the cocaine found at the Wigan home was 81 per cent pure, while some was cut with creatine powder Glynn, 63, was convicted of being concerned in the supply of heroin and cocaine by a jury in September. A judge let her walk free from court on a suspended prison sentence, telling her there was 'very little evidence of [her] having a management function in the chain or controlli He added: "You have physical ailments and your son and bereaved mother are dependent on you." Manchester Crown Court earlier heard officer swooped on Glynn's Collett Close home, in the Scholes area of the borough, in April 2021 following a tip-off that drugs were being supplied f She had lived there for 27 years. "She said she shared the property with her ex-partner... but when police entered she was there alone," prosecution barrister Craig McGregor Glynn said

He'd already been jailed for dealing The £1m-a-year racket flooded the streets of the town with crack cocaine and heroin, surviving a series of police operations to bring it down In 2024, two 'untouchable' dealers were the latest to be jailed for running the line, first exposed in the BBC series The Detectives: Taking Down An OCG which shined a light on the gang, based in Newbold, Rochdale. The drugs line became active again within hours of the pair being Ali, 34, was a familiar face on the scene. He was jailed in 2015 after admitting conspiracy to supply heroin and cocaine - one of 13 dealers locked up following an undercover operation In its latest incarnation, Ali - known as 'The Ghost' - ran the 'Adam' line, until he and two others were caught. Monday (November 9), he was jailed for 10 years and six months

Firefighters were called to Elsa Recycling on Station Road in Reddish this morning It's thought bundles of paper being stored in the yard set alight. Plumes of black smoke were pictured billowing from the blaze Station Road is also thought to have been closed while firefighters battled the flames. Witness Rob Larkin, who works nearby, said he feared the fire was going to spread He said: "The buildings are probably 20ft high and the flames were reaching that high. evidence_packet.evidence_text: ‘Oh how nice for Marple, what about Hazel Grove? Nothing !!!’ Everything seems to be going Marple’s way. It’s no surprise that Agatha Christie named her teacup sleuth after these parts. The 13,000-strong town in the southeastern corner of Greater Manchester is England in its cosiest pastoral garb: a network of canal walks and independent sh Once a retirement haven, now young professionals are decamping from the city, drawn by sourdough and the countryside. The high street of bygone Marple has been subsumed by a score of flourishing independents. A greasy spoon once plainly boasting “Hot And Cold Sandwiches” has beco And the biggest change is still to come. In December, the town will unveil its £20m Marple Hub: a sustainable red-brick, glazed complex with a new library, a five-lane swimming pool, a gym, a clinic and a cafe. Most of it paid for by Levelling Up cash “Oh how nice for Marple, what about Hazel Grove? Nothing !!!” one Facebook user wrote. “Lovely for Marple! What about Reddish Baths?” Meanwhile, a Marple resident was asking for an update on the council’s plans for a sauna So, one of the richest areas in Stockport gets a pool with a moving floor, while trees grow out of the side of the rotting library in Reddish

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester will come together under one sky this weekend as free fireworks celebrations return to light up the night sky on Saturday 7 November at three Manchester parks: Heaton Park, Wythenshawe Park and Platt Fields Park This year's events have been designed with sustainability, affordability and accessibility at their heart, ensuring the celebrations can be enjoyed by as many people as possible Affordability is a key focus, with a range of free activities and entertainment on offer throughout the evening and people are encouraged to take part in the Lantern Parade at 7pm prior to the main firework display. Visitors can also enjoy value-for-money funfair rides, with 95% The events have been planned to cater for a wide audience, including those who would prefer to attend an earlier, shorter, lower-noise display. Hosting three large-scale events across the city also helps reduce the environmental impact associated with multiple smaller community d A number of measures have been introduced to improve sustainability. Avoidable single-use plastics have been removed from all event sites, the pyrotechnics supplier uses sustainable packaging, and post-event litter picks will take place immediately after the celebrations. Local s In a bid to reduce food waste, any surplus food will, where possible, be redistributed through local charities and community projects in partnership with the Our Manchester Food Partnership

evidence_packet.evidence_text: People are invited to step forward and make a difference in their community Anyone interested in representing local residents and helping to make decisions affecting the area are invited to consider putting themselves forward as a candidate for the Royton North By-Election. If there is only one candidate nominated, then that candidate would be elected without contest. If more than one valid nomination is received, residents will go to the polls on Thursday 3 December 2026 to elect thei This is an opportunity for local people from all backgrounds to represent the interests of their community, raise issues that matter to residents and play a direct role in shaping the future of Royton North and the wider borough. Councillors represent the Council to the community Anyone wishing to stand for election can obtain a nomination pack from the Elections Office at the J.R.Clynes Building, Cultural Quarter, Greaves Street, Oldham, OL1 1AL, between 9am and 5pm, or they can be emailed on request by emailing election@oldham.gov.uk Completed nomination papers must be submitted in person and cannot be accepted by email, post, fax or any other electronic method. Papers can be delivered to the J.R.Clynes Building between 10am and 4pm and no later than 4pm on Friday 6 November

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre Sona Jobarteh is the first professional female kora virtuoso to emerge from any of West Africa’s five Griot dynasties, and a singer, composer and bandleader whose concerts fill some of the world’s finest halls. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. evidence_packet.summary: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live […] The post Beat the Jams Autumn season announced appeared first on Band on the Wall
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. At Counter, he challenges convention by exploring what British cooking can The menu puts this philosophy into practice with dishes that combine unexpected ingredients and inventive flavour pairings. Highlights include the Beef Tartare Pressed Croissant, pairing aged beef with a crispy pressed croissant, smoked oyster mayo, wasabi and pickled shallot and From the grill, guests can enjoy the Satay Spatchcock Chicken, served with peanut satay, fermented chilli, coconut, burnt lime and crispy shallot, alongside the slow-cooked Thai Lamb Shoulder, served with red thai sauce, chilli and coriander

evidence_packet.lead: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities.
evidence_packet.summary: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The plan sets out an ambition to create 200,000 entry-level jobs, including apprenticeships, during that period The plan also addresses how AI is changing workforce requirements and the importance of ensuring people entering the industry have both technical knowledge and practical workplace skills Manchester Digital's 2026 Sector Insights Report highlighted a reduction of around 20% in early-career opportunities, despite continued demand for experienced technology professionals

It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and t
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester City FC 'Lazy' Man City charges theory rejected as Premier League punishment wait continues amid appeal Manchester City were found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges that the Premier League alleged they had broken between 2009 and 2018 Add to preferred sou A sport integrity expert has insisted that a delay publishing Manchester City's punishment for breaking the Premier League 's financial rules is not down to the decision makers being 'lazy'. Back in September, it was confirmed that City had been found guilty of nearly all of the The independent panel found City had intended to breach financial rules by inflating revenues or reducing costs by more than £900m, through a series of 'sham' arrangements. City have appealed the decision and have reiterated their innocence As the appeal process continues, City fans have nervously been waiting for their club's punishment. Due to the number of charges and the unprecedented nature of the case, several 'likely' punishments have been discussed including; hefty points deductions, transfer bans, expulsion Get all the best Man City news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the MEN! evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester City FC Man City have obvious decision to make on Abdukodir Khusanov Manchester City defender Abdukodir Khusanov has been one of the players used most by Enzo Maresca so far Add to preferred sources Comments Sport Simon Bajkowski Chief Manchester City Wr Three months into Manchester City under Enzo Maresca and the manager has leaned on some players more than others. While Gianluigi Donnarumma has played more minutes than anybody else, the five outfield players with the most minutes are interesting Ruben Dias leads the way followed by his vice-captain Erling Haaland , with both having clearly defined roles in the team. Next comes Elliot Anderson, who has been essential in the midfield, and Marc Guehi is still up there despite some early substitutions recently Coming in after Guehi, having recently leapfrogged Josko Gvardiol, is Uzbek defender Abdukodir Khusanov . Despite it not feeling like his place in the team is nailed, the 22-year-old has been turned to repeatedly by Maresca across the backline Get all the best Man City news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the MEN! That speaks to his versatility, and one of the reasons the club opted not to sign a right-back in the summer was because they felt that Khusanov could deputise for Matheus Nunes. Given the way Maresca likes to build up with three centre-backs, Khusanov could be even more valuable

Lille would not budge from their price all summer and, after months of trying to Lille had been determined to keep the Moroccan teenager for another year and willing to agree more favourable terms with any club who would give him back to them for the season. City, however, paid a premium because they were convinced he was ready and some at the club indicated It didn't take long for Bouaddi to meet the hype, coming in for Elliot Anderson in Porto and guiding City to an important away win in their first Champions League game "Tonight he was very good, you expect from Erling, Ruben, Mateo that they can manage these kind of games better but you don't expect it from a guy of 18," said Enzo Maresca. evidence_packet.lead: Manchester City defender Marc Guehi was replaced at half time during the Blues' 3-1 Premier League defeat to Nottingham Forest
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester City defender Marc Guehi was replaced at half time during the Blues' 3-1 Premier League defeat to Nottingham Forest
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester City FC Man City release Marc Guehi statement amid defensive injury issues Manchester City defender Marc Guehi was replaced at half time during the Blues' 3-1 Premier League defeat to Nottingham Forest Add to preferred sources Comments Sport Jack Flintha Manchester City have confirmed that Marc Guehi will be remaining at the Etihad Campus during the international break after withdrawing from the England squad. Guehi had been called up to Thomas Tuchel's 25-man squad for the fixtures against Croatia and Spain in the Nations League On Saturday, he was replaced at half time in what looked to be a tactical change. However, Enzo Maresca confirmed post-match that Guehi had asked to come off with a suspected injury. He has now withdrawn from te Endland squad and been replaced by Newcastle United's Dan Burn. City "Guehi was named in Thomas Tuchel’s original 25-man group, along with fellow City star Elliot Anderson, for UEFA Nations League meetings with Croatia and Spain," they wrote on the club's website. "Our No.6 will instead remain with the club ahead of the return of domestic football Get all the best Man City news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the MEN! Guehi's withdrawal from the England squad compounds City's injury concerns following Saturday's defeat. Maresca also confirmed at the City Ground that Josko Gvardiol had asked to be replaced having felt a 'small issue' during the week

evidence_packet.evidence_text: 27 ноября 2026 года в Studio 338 состоится концерт VOLKANOV в Лондоне Первый вечерний туман над Темзой, отражение городских огней на воде, аромат кофе из маленьких лондонских кофейных и спешка многолюдных улиц — всё это обладает удивительной способностью вдруг остановить время и вернуть к самым ценным воспоминаниям. Так рождаются чувства, которые д Лондон — город, где встречаются десятки культур, языков и человеческих историй, где старинные набережные Темзы соседствуют с современными кварталами, а бешеный ритм мегаполиса не мешает беречь особую атмосферу уюта. В конце ноября именно здесь, вдали от дома, искренние композиции Концерты Дмитрия Волканова — это искренняя встреча, где между артистом и слушателями почти не остается дистанции. Стоит только прозвучать первым аккордам, как незнакомые люди начинают улыбаться друг другу, петь в унисон и чувствовать себя большой семьей, которую объединила музыка Когда к концу вечера Лондон окутает прохлада, сцена Studio 338 впервые встретит Дмитрия Волканова. Этот вечер станет особым событием — первым знакомством артиста с лондонской публикой. Вас ждут искренние песни, теплая атмосфера и мощная энергетика! Презентація максі-синглу "Живий" Кожного разу, коли перед менеджментом гурту Бумбокс стоїть завдання написати пресреліз, ми починаємо згадувати цікаві факти. Скільки концертів зіграли, скільки грошей зібрали, які пісні видали. Це база. Непогано ще пам’ятати, чи був гурт у країні, до якої ми збираємося, чи це пер О, як би хотілося написати: "Концерт гурту Бумбокс" — і як у Львові за добу продано 8000 квитків. Так-так, ми не про Львів розповідаємо, хоча теж про Європу Наші віддані слухачі, якщо ви перебуваєте за кордоном, сподіваємось, вам буде цікаво дізнатися, що після традиційної перерви на декілька місяців, Бумбокс поїде в турне від Ізраїлю до Німеччини, від Англії до Польщі, від Ірландії до Словаччини та Чехії І повеземо ми в це турне свіженький, як херсонський кавун, максі-сингл “Живий”, підсилений піснями з різних альбомів, під частину яких виросли ви, а під частину зростають ваші діти Тож ознайомтеся, будь ласка, уважно з розкладом туру, купуйте квитки заздалегідь, готуйте гроші на донати та мерч — зустрінемося в листопаді
